name: Mexican Tomato Soup
author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors

ingredients.item: About ½ L tomato sauce, tomato purée, or similar
¼ cup (60 ml) vegetable or olive oil
More vegetables according to your taste

steps: Cut onion fine and fry lightly in a large saucepan with a bit of oil.
Add vegetables, roughly in the order you find logical (ie, tomatoes don't take long, peppers can be there from the start).

Add about ½ tsp salt, adjusting to taste. The salt will extract water from the vegetables and make them 'stew' faster. You can cover the pot if it goes slowly—once again, this slows the evaporation and allows the vegetables to cook in the water they lose themselves.

Add salt and sugar to taste. Be bold; tomato sauce takes a lot of salt and at least a heaping tsp of sugar to taste right. If unsure, separate a small amount and try adding more salt—you will see the tastes changes significantly.
Serve with tortilla chips, or toasted bread if not available.

culture.text: Mexican tomato soup is a very simple dish that can be made hot if wanted. It is very nutritious for a soup too.
